heroSummary: The Creality K1 Max handles Prusament PC Blend effectively within its fully enclosed build chamber up to a maximum reliable speed of 143 mm/s capped by a 12 mm³/s volumetric limit. Due to the printer's 100°C maximum bed temperature falling just below Prusament's ideal 105–115°C range, strict chamber preheating and high-performance adhesives are mandatory.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Smooth or Textured PEI Plate with a generous layer of PVP glue stick or Magigoo PC as a release/adhesion agent
slicerTweaks: Set Max Volumetric Speed to 12 mm³/s in OrcaSlicer filament settings to prevent extruder skipping and maintain 143 mm/s maximum print velocity.
Limit Part Cooling Fan to 0% standard and 20% max for short layer times under 15 seconds to eliminate catastrophic delamination.
Configure a 5-10mm outer brim with a 0.0mm brim-object gap to mechanically anchor sharp corners against warping at the 100°C bed limit.
Enable OrcaSlicer Pressure Advance at 0.035s and calibrate flow ratio to approximately 0.96 to manage high melt viscosity and corner bulging.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Corner lifting and severe warping from build plate
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Bed temperature limited to 100°C while chamber thermal gradients create high mechanical contraction stress.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply Magigoo PC or fresh glue stick, enable a 10mm outer brim, and preheat the chamber to at least 45-50°C for 20 minutes before printing.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Interlayer splitting or cracking during or after print
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling or printing with the top cover removed, allowing cold air drafts into the chamber.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Keep the K1 Max top glass and door completely closed, turn the side auxiliary fan OFF, and limit part cooling fan to 0-20%.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Rough surface finish, stringing, and extruder clicking
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Moisture absorption in hygroscopic PC filament or exceeding the 12 mm³/s volumetric melt threshold.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament in a blast-drying oven at 75-80°C for at least 8 hours and ensure hotend temperature is set to 275-280°C.

faq.question: Can the K1 Max bed reach the manufacturer's recommended 110°C for Prusament PC Blend?
faq.answer: No, the Creality K1 Max firmware and hardware cap the heatbed at 100°C. You must compensate for this slight shortfall by using a dedicated adhesive such as Magigoo PC and pre-soaking the chamber.

faq.question: Do I need an aftermarket hardened nozzle to print standard Prusament PC Blend?
faq.answer: No, non-carbon Prusament PC Blend is non-abrasive and the K1 Max already ships with a hardened steel-tipped nozzle capable of handling 300°C.

faq.question: Should I keep the K1 Max top lid installed or off during this print?
faq.answer: Keep the top glass lid and front door strictly closed. Polycarbonate requires high ambient chamber temperatures and zero drafts to prevent thermal shock and layer cracking.

faq.question: Can I run the auxiliary chamber fan on the side of the K1 Max?
faq.answer: No, completely disable the auxiliary side fan in OrcaSlicer. Direct cool air from the side fan causes immediate warping, thermal shock, and layer delamination in PC prints.
